description: Tests the Legal Clearance agent's judgment rather than simple keyword matching. Some real-world references are genuinely risky; others are trivial, generic, or already-cleared use and should be treated as low/no risk.
scenes: SCENE 1 - INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY. Priya scrolls through her phone, an unbranded generic smartphone, and mentions offhand that she 'should really switch to an iPhone someday.'
SCENE 2 - INT. OFFICE - DAY. Priya's boss says, 'Get me on a call with Sundar Pichai directly, I don't care how,' in an exasperated, clearly exaggerated tone about wanting to escalate a complaint.
SCENE 3 - INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT. Priya's roommate drinks from a plain red soda can with no visible branding, referred to only as 'a soda.'
SCENE 4 - INT. CAR - DAY. Priya's father proudly says he's driven the same Toyota Corolla for fifteen years and it's never once broken down, praising the brand by name at length.

SCENE 5 - EXT. STADIUM - NIGHT. A crowd chants a chant closely mirroring a real, currently-active national cricket team's well-known signature chant, word for word, in a scene clearly depicting a real upcoming tournament match by name and date.

SCENE 6 - INT. BEDROOM - NIGHT. Priya's younger brother has a poster on his wall of a clearly recognizable, still-in-production animated character from a major studio franchise, described in enough visual detail (colors, exact costume, logo) to be unambiguous.
SCENE 7 - INT. CAFE - DAY. Priya mentions she's a big fan of 'a famous singer,' left deliberately unnamed and generic, with no identifying details given.

ground_truth.description: Scene 1's iPhone mention is a single, brief, generic aspirational reference — low risk, arguably not worth a strong flag.
Scene 2 names a real, identifiable real person (Sundar Pichai) directly in dialogue in a context that could imply his personal involvement — worth a flag even though it's brief and exaggerated.
Scene 3's unbranded soda can has no identifiable brand or trademark — should not be flagged.
Scene 4's extended, named, positive brand endorsement (Toyota Corolla) goes beyond incidental use and edges toward implied endorsement — worth flagging for clearance review.
Scene 5 combines a real sports organization's likely-trademarked chant with a real, named, dated tournament — higher risk requiring clearance.
Scene 6 describes copyrighted IP (a specific studio character) in enough visual detail to constitute clear infringement risk, not just an incidental mention.
Scene 7 deliberately avoids naming any real person — should not be flagged.
